_comment: ai-slop-lint: ignore-file. Data for scripts/ai_slop_lint.py. Tier 1 is banned outright; tier 2 is capped by density. Source for the vocabulary: r/ClaudeAI 'Favorite Claudeisms, in no particular order' (197 comments), saved by the author to 01-inbox/ai-writing-skill.md on 2026-07-23. Design: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-28-ai-slop-filter-design.md. v2 (certainty, coined_names, headings, rather than / instead of): docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-07-ai-slop-linter-v2-design.md. v3 (shared, jobs, banned_devices, six rhetoric hints): docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-18-artifact-copy-gate-design.md. jobs holds one block per copy job and nothing else, so it can be iterated: caps are word counts per element kind, off lists the hit labels that job drops (Persuade drops closing-beat, the author's decision 10 on 9/18), and em-dash there also switches off the over-cap pass, which makes no hit. rhetoric holds one id and its pattern per entry, nothing else, so it can be iterated: Hints the carrier test gates, applied per sentence in rhetoric.py rather than per line. Antithesis moved here on 9/18: the plain regex read "Rai is his son, not his daughter" and "a clean open, not a verdict" the same way, and the first is a correction that names a person. A sentence carrying a name, a time, a number or a quote keeps its X-not-Y. Adding a phrase is a data edit; do not move phrases into the linter.

tier1._note: Banned outright. Match is case-insensitive, whole-phrase, word-boundary anchored.
phrases: i am going to be honest
doing a lot of quiet work
now i have the full picture
now i have the complete picture

literal._note: A tier-1 phrase with an honest literal sense is spared when this regex matches the text right after it. From Bronsdon's avoid-ai-writing (2026), which flags load-bearing only before an abstract noun. Added 2026-09-27; checked on 'The beam is load-bearing for the 2nd floor'.

tier2._note: Real words over-reached for. per_phrase_per_1000 is the cap for any single phrase; total_per_1000 caps the whole tier. Both are hits per 1000 words of linted prose. genuinely through navigate the complexities came in on 2026-09-27 from the audit of the awesome-claude-code writing skills (docs/reviews/2026-09-27-ai-filter-vs-community-skills.md). delve and underscore moved here from shared.academic, which only reads Prove, so a Tell note saying them was never flagged. genuinely is capped, not banned: 9 uses in the author's own notes. pivotal came out the same day: 1 hit in his journal against 1 in 308,577 machine words.

structural._note: Regex hints for the two rules the 2026-07-28 miss exposed, plus the CLAUDE.md rules a regex can reach. Each is a HINT: it marks a candidate for the judgment pass, and the skill decides. Patterns are applied case-insensitively to prose lines only.

rules.label: The reframe: denies a reading, substitutes a subtler one, adds no fact
rules.pattern: (?:^|(?<=[.!?]\s))not\s+\w+\.\s+\w|isn['’]?t\s+\w+\s+so much as|it['’]?s not (?:that )?\w+[,.]? (?:it['’]?s|so much as)|\b(?:don['’]?t|do not|stop) call(?:ing)? it\b[^.]{1,40}\.\s+call it\b

rules.label: Trailing clause asserting importance with no evidence
rules.pattern: , which is (?:a |the )?(?:different|quieter|real|whole|entire|interesting|important)\b|\band that matters\b|\bwhich is the (?:point|whole point)\b|\band that['’]?s (?:the|what) (?:point|matters)\b|\band a (?:different|quieter|louder|bigger|smaller|stranger|sadder|worse|better|stronger) one\b|\bis the (?:interesting|important|real|telling|revealing|cleanest|clearest) (?:one|part|bit|thing|instance)\b|\b(?:that|which) is exactly what\b|\bin miniature\b|, (?:highlighting|underscoring|showcasing|emphasi[sz]ing|cementing|reinforcing|signall?ing)\b

rules.label: "Here's what/the thing" as a transition
rules.pattern: \bhere['’]?s (?:what|the thing|why|how it works)\b|(?:^\W*|(?<=[.!?]\s))(?:it )?turns out\b|\bthe real story (?:is|here)\b

rules.label: Self-questioning transition
rules.pattern: \bso what does (?:this|that) mean\b|\bwhat does (?:this|that) actually mean\b|\bwhy does (?:this|that) matter\b

rules.label: "I'm sitting with these questions:" followed by bullets
Says it while claiming not to
rules.pattern: \bnot to mention\b|\bneedless to say\b|\bto say nothing of\b|\bI won['’]?t (?:even )?(?:mention|go into)\b

rules.label: Trails off instead of saying it
Affirms by denying the opposite; say the size
"Full stop." closing a sentence for emphasis; the word as typography is fine
'As X put it': the source dressed up instead of named
Colon hinge: the left side labels what the right side says (Roxby's Style Patch, 2026). Say it as one sentence
'The honest X' as an intensifier: the honest next move, reading, test. 13 in the briefs on 2026-09-27; judgment nouns only, since the author wrote 'the honest state of my relationship' in his journal
Two hedges on one claim: could potentially, may eventually (Bronsdon's avoid-ai-writing, 2026). Keep one

certainty._note: Certainty words. Each is a STRUCT hint only when the sentence carrying it has no number, name, quote or source; the gate is the thin-sentence carrier test on the sentence's own span, with the word itself blanked so a sentence-initial 'Clearly' never reads as a name. From the portfolio style guide 2.3. Measured 9/7 before gating over 628 machine notes: clearly 22, proves 16, reliably 11. 'never' and 'always' are left out on purpose: 'never' appears 715 times and nearly all of it is honest.

coined_names._note: A Title Case phrase of 2 to 4 words ending in one of `suffixes` is a STRUCT hint unless it, or its right-aligned tail, is a vault note name (read from the filenames under `vault_dirs` at run time, so the rule follows the author's folders) or is in `known` (products). `vault_dirs` is every vault folder the author authors, read recursively: the capture, project and area folders, the six 04-resources subfolders that hold notes he titles, and 05-archive. Left out on purpose: 04-resources/journal, feed, daily-execution, daily-thought-analysis, research and instruments, which hold captures and machine output rather than titles he coined. The first list was 02-projects and 03-areas only, and on 9/7 that flagged 04-resources/reference/fitness-system.md and 04-resources/reference/multipass-system.md, 7 hits each, as machine-coined names. From the guide 1.4 and 3.3: name a pattern when it is validated, never when it is exciting. 'Social System' (42 hits on 9/7) is machine-coined; 'Meta Layer System' (25) is his note.

density._note: Non-phrase counts measured over prose only. The em-dash cap is a style limit the author chose, not a sign a machine wrote the text: Bronsdon's avoid-ai-writing corpus (2026) found em dashes in 9.9% of human documents against 1.9% of machine ones. Keep it; stop citing it as an AI tell.

shared._note: Slop words, each list with the jobs it runs in. forms: stock feedback phrases from the 9/18 settings-form run. academic: the lexicon the 9/18 paper run missed. pep_talk: empty-state cheer. sell: the selling words the 9/18 deck and feature-grid runs let through, matched with -s, -ed and -ing endings, and -ly on the words ending -less, -ful or -ive (seamlessly, powerfully; never potentially). jobs is decision 13 in the 2026-09-18 spec, confirmed by the author on 9/23: sell reads Show and Persuade, academic reads Prove, forms and pep_talk read all four. Widen a jobs line to all four jobs to flip it back. On a prose or subtext row a capitalised match inside a sentence is a name and is skipped (Empower Semiconductor, Hub); at a sentence start it still counts. A heading row is left to pitch-heading, which reads sell in every job: the headings block that held its own 15 words, all of them in sell, came out on 9/19. It had 22 hits on 9/7, every one '## The leverage point' in June and July thought analyses. innovation, ai-powered, cloud-native and all-in-one came in on 9/27 from the naming skill (GlacierPhonk, 2026); platform, solutions and transformation were left out because pitch-heading reads sell in every job and '## Platforms' and '### Proposed Solution' are honest headings here.

mention_cues._note: A word in single or double quotes is a mention, and the shared lists skip it, when the quote holds two or more words (speech, a title) or when one of these sits within three words in front of a one-word quote: the word 'synergy'. A lone quoted word with no cue is a scare quote and still counts. Round 2 of the 9/18 task 7 review.
